title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The UK government has issued its response to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards. It outlines actions to improve AI accountability, safety and transparency while encouraging collaboration across public and private sectors.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out rules to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector, aiming to keep assessments fair, secure and trustworthy. The policy outlines guidelines for exam boards, teachers and candidates, and encourages cooperation with government and industry to monitor AI’s effects.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how using copyrighted works to train and develop AI systems impacts creators, consumers, and the economy. It also discusses legal challenges and suggests ways to balance technological progress with protecting intellectual property rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has responded to the House of Lords Select Committee’s report “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency,” outlining its commitment to boosting AI research, regulation, and workforce skills. It pledges to strengthen oversight, promote ethical standards, and ensure the UK remains a global leader in responsible AI development.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: These terms of reference outline the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee tasked with reviewing how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards. The accompanying FAQs explain key concepts, answer common questions, and guide stakeholders through the review process.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of artificial intelligence. The submission outlines the organization’s views on how AI should be regulated and governed.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines how the organisation aims to become the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑driven defence force in the world given its size. It focuses on developing cutting‑edge AI capabilities, ensuring robust governance, and fostering collaboration across defence and industry to meet national security goals.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy looks at how artificial intelligence changes the rules that govern medical products, especially in terms of safety and effectiveness. It uses the principles laid out in the AI White Paper to guide the development, approval, and ongoing monitoring of AI‑driven medical devices and treatments.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to take advantage of artificial intelligence technologies. It also outlines how they will identify and manage the risks that AI could bring to safety, privacy and infrastructure.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report outlines how copyright‑protected works are used in training and developing AI systems, focusing on compliance with Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It provides an update on current practices, challenges, and regulatory progress to ensure that AI development respects copyright laws.
